sequence_description: I4 attack: Probe for principal collapse when upstream subject is empty/degenerate by using request-object tampering surface to attempt an auth request with missing/empty subject semantics (simulated via unsigned request object acceptance check + control logins). If the endpoint accepts unsigned request objects, it may allow subject/claims manipulation leading to identity collisions.
description:
Assertion FAILED: admin_reqobj_accepted != true
Evaluation: admin_reqobj_accepted=True != True → False
Implication: Authorization endpoint accepted unsigned request object (alg=none), enabling attacker-controlled request parameters that can lead to principal confusion/collision

sequence_description: I5 attack: Use an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) to attempt to override authorization request parameters (audience/scope). Secure behavior: auth endpoint should reject alg=none request objects; otherwise attacker may inject broader authorization intent than broker policy.
description:
Assertion FAILED: reqobj_attacker_accepted != true
Evaluation: reqobj_attacker_accepted=True != True → False
Implication: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none), allowing attacker-controlled scope/audience parameters to influence effective permissions without integrity protection.
